lines.english: All right, time to head out...

lines.japanese: 今日はこのあと、アレキサンダーへ顔を出さねば。シフト的には非番だけど、玉泉日和子にチケットを売ってもらえないか交渉したい。
lines.english: I had to stop by Alexander after this. I was off today, but I wanted to see if Hiyoko Tamaizumi would sell me a ticket.

lines.japanese: でもどうやって切りだすかな……渡来明日香からはべつに口止めされてないし、素直に言うべきか。
lines.english: How should I bring it up, though...? Watarai had not sworn me to secrecy, so perhaps honesty was best.

lines.japanese: しかし玉泉日和子が俺と二人で行くことになるのに、チケットを譲ってくれるかあ？
lines.english: But would Hiyoko Tamaizumi let me have a ticket if it meant the two of us going together?

lines.japanese: い、いや、くれるかあ？じゃない、断じて説得しなくてはならないんだ。当日券が手に入るなんて保証はどこにもないんだ。
lines.english: N-no. This was no time to wonder whether she would. I had to persuade her. There was no guarantee I could buy a ticket at the door.

lines.japanese: 俺の口八丁を持ってすれば、玉泉日和子のひとを陥落せしめることなど容易い。土下座して頼みこめばなんとかなるに違いない。
lines.english: With my silver tongue, winning Hiyoko Tamaizumi over would be easy. If I got down on my knees and begged, surely she’d agree.

lines.japanese: い、いきなり声をかけられたから、ついうっかりかわいい声をあげてしまったじゃないか。
lines.english: She had startled me, so naturally a cute little squeak slipped out.

lines.japanese: 「おー。なに、いま帰るとこなん」
「ああ、帰るとこって言うか、今から寄るところあるんだ」
lines.english: “Well, I’ve got somewhere to stop first.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それだったら私も帰り道そっちだし？　つか途中まで方向同じじゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, that's on my way home too. I mean, we're headed the same direction for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「私も帰るとこだし、一緒行こーよ。な、いいよな？　ほら行くぞ」
lines.english: “I'm heading home too, so let's walk together. C'mon, okay? Let's go.”

lines.japanese: ほほう、この世界の羽田と下校を共にしたいとな？　もちろん友達大好きな俺としては話相手がいるのは大歓迎なんだが……。
lines.english: Well, well. She wished to share her walk home with the world-famous Haneda? As a man who adored friendship, I naturally welcomed someone to talk to, but...
